findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff defines `downsize` twice, and the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts) replaces the first (from, to, max_width, max_height), so every existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 3..4). Any existing code path calling OptimizedImage.downsize with separate width/height args (thumbnail generation, cooking pipelines) crashes with ArgumentError as soon as this file loads, breaking all image thumbnailing on the site.

[BUG] The downsize loop passes "80%" as the dimensions argument to OptimizedImage.downsize, but downsize_instructions (and downsize_instructions_animated) build a geometry string from width/height and will not interpret a bare percent, so the ImageMagick command is malformed or a no-op and the file never shrinks. The loop runs 5 iterations without reducing tempfile.size below max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, then Upload.create_for proceeds with an oversized file, which fails server-side with the same 'file too large' error the feature was supposed to eliminate — the feature silently does nothing.

[BUG] The loop downsizes in place (from == to: tempfile.path passed as both source and destination), and ImageMagick `convert in.gif out.gif` with identical input/output paths truncates the file mid-read, producing a corrupt/empty image when a single pass would have sufficed. Users uploading large GIFs get a corrupted upload stored and served instead of a downsized one.

[ADVISORY] FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is fed a filename derived from File.basename(URI.parse(url).path) for API URL uploads, which is empty or extension-less for URLs like 'https://host/image?id=1', so the image check fails and large remote images are never downsized. API clients pulling oversized images by URL bypass the downsize path entirely and get the old hard-size failure.

[ADVISORY] The client now hardcodes 10MB while the server still enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so on any site where max_image_size_kb > 10240 the client blocks uploads the server would accept, and where it is lower the server rejects files the client let through. Admins who raise or lower max_image_size_kb get contradictory behavior between the client pre-check and the server; users see the wrong limit in the error message shown for 413 responses.

[BUG] The new 3-argument def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) defined after the 4-argument version silently replaces it in Ruby, so every existing caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) with integer width/height now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 3) — or, where callers pass geometry strings, the surviving 4-arg code path is dead. All existing thumbnail/optimized-image generation call sites that pass separate width and height integers crash with ArgumentError at runtime, breaking avatar/thumbnail generation site-wide, not just the new upload path.

[BUG] The client hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024, discarding SiteSetting max_<type>_size_kb, so the client-side gate and error message no longer match the server-side limit for any admin-configured value. On sites where max_image_size_kb (or another type's setting) is below 10MB, non-image uploads above the real setting pass the client check and then fail server-side with a generic error, and users are shown '10 MB' in the file_too_large message even though the actual limit is lower.

[BUG] The auto-downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of 80% scaling (0.8^5 ≈ 33% of original area), so any image larger than ~3x the configured max_image_size_kb exits the loop still over the limit and the upload fails anyway — the feature's promise of 'automatically downsize large images' silently fails for exactly the largest images it targets. Users uploading e.g. a 12MB image to a site with max_image_size_kb = 2048 (2MB) still get a rejection after 5 wasteful synchronous convert invocations, with no indication the system tried or why the advertised auto-downsize did not apply.

[ADVISORY] The image-type gate is FileHelper.is_image?(filename), where filename is File.basename(URI.parse(url).path) for API URL downloads — a URL without an extension (or with a query-style image endpoint) yields a filename is_image? rejects, so no downsize occurs and the oversized download still fails. API consumers uploading image URLs lacking extensions get the old hard-fail behavior inconsistently with multipart uploads of the same image; also SVGs (if is_image? matches them) are passed to convert's downsize path which cannot rasterize them.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) downsizes in-place, so if convert fails mid-write the original upload file is destroyed or truncated and the corrupted tempfile is passed to Upload.create_for instead of the original bytes. A transient ImageMagick failure during downsize corrupts the user's upload irrecoverably on a path that previously never mutated the uploaded file; the user gets an opaque upload error and must re-upload.

[ADVISORY] The new auto-downsize behavior in uploads_controller has no test coverage in this diff — no spec file touches create_upload's downsize loop (no changes under spec/ exist in the diff), so the loop bound, the SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 guard, and the animated-image allow_animation flag path are all unverified. A regression in the downsize loop (e.g. the Argumenterror from the overloaded OptimizedImage.downsize signature) would ship undetected; the guard for max_image_size_kb = 0 (unlimited) is untested and its intended semantics undefined.

[BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same module — the second definition (line 149) silently replaces the first (line 143), so every existing caller invoking `downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` with two numeric dimension arguments now hits the new one-`dimensions`-string signature. Any existing call site like `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, to, 100, 100)` raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 3..4) or builds a broken ImageMagick instruction, breaking avatar/thumbnail resizing paths unrelated to this feature.

[BUG] The client-side file size check replaces the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, which is unrelated work traceable to no requirement in 'automatically downsize large images'. Admins who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB still see uploads up to 10MB pass the client gate, and the setting's UI becomes a silent no-op for client validation — behavior change unrequested by the stated intent.

[BUG] The API-URL download limit is hardcoded to `10.megabytes`, replacing `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, decoupling the server-side limit from site configuration without any stated requirement. An admin who lowers max_image_size_kb to e.g. 1MB still has the API URL-download path fetching files up to 10MB into a tempfile, defeating the configured limit on that path and contradicting the downsize logic two lines below which uses the SiteSetting.

[ADVISORY] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB as the reported max size, but the server's actual enforced limit (after the new downsize loop) is `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` plus the result of up to 5 downsizing iterations, so the message shown to users is not the server's real limit. Users uploading a 9MB image on a site with max_image_size_kb set to 500KB see the client pass the file, the server's 5 failed downsize iterations reject it, and then a 413 dialog telling them 10MB was the limit — a wrong, unactionable error message.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passing a percentage string where the (overwritten) downsize signature expects a `WxH` dimensions string, and the non-animated path builds `downsize_instructions` with a `dimensions` parameter the existing instruction builder formats as `WxH` geometry. For non-GIF images the resulting ImageMagick geometry string is malformed (or `80%` is passed through only by luck of convert syntax), so images either fail to downsize — leaving a >max upload that the 5-iteration loop silently gives up on — or are downsized once, never checked against the setting's intent; the failure is silent because convert errors are swallowed.

[BUG] The diff defines `downsize` twice in the same module, and the later `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overrides the earlier `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` definition, so the earlier overload is dead code. Every existing caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` (the thumbnail/post-image paths throughout the codebase) now binds `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` — an Integer — so `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` raises TypeError (Integer#[] takes an Integer, not a Symbol), crashing all thumbnail generation for non-animated images.

[BUG] The client hardcodes `10 * 1024` as the upload limit, discarding the per-type server setting `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` and severing the client/server single source of truth. An admin who raises `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB still gets every client-side upload rejected at 10MB with a wrong error message; and with the new server-side downsizing, the client now blocks exactly the uploads this feature was built to accept. The 10MB literal drifts independently from the three other hardcoded copies in this diff.

[BUG] The downsize loop repeatedly scales the image by a fixed '80%' up to 5 times and gives up silently when the file is still over the limit, so `Upload.create_for` is then called with a still-too-large file. A PNG or animation whose compressed size does not shrink proportionally with dimensions (palette-heavy PNGs, animated GIFs) exits the loop after 5 attempts still over `max_image_size_kb`, and the upload then fails with the same unhelpful oversized error the feature was supposed to eliminate — while also having needlessly degraded a merely-slightly-over-limit image to ~33% of its area (0.8^5) even when one 95% step would have sufficed.

[BUG] The loop gates animation preservation on `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` when the relevant setting for uploaded content is `allow_animated_uploads` — a confusable-pair binding. On sites with animated uploads allowed but animated thumbnails disabled, a user's uploaded animated GIF is collapsed to a static frame by the downsize loop even though site policy permits animated uploads, silently destroying the user's content.

[BUG] The downsize operates in place on the user's tempfile (`tempfile.path` as both from and to) via a shell `convert` invocation with no atomic temp output, and the original uploaded bytes are unconditionally discarded. The user's original high-resolution image is permanently lost before `Upload.create_for` records anything: if the downsize succeeds but the upload fails for any other reason (sha/duplicate, DB error), the original is unrecoverable; and in-place `convert input output` on the same path risks a truncated/corrupt file on ImageMagick versions that stream reads, which `convert_with`'s exit-status check would then upload as a corrupt image.

[ADVISORY] The URL-download path replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, silently capping API-provided URL downloads below the configured server limit. Admins who raise `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB get API uploads from URLs silently truncated-at-download behavior (FileHelper.download aborts the fetch over 10MB) with no setting able to control it; the three copies of '10MB' in this diff (utilities.js x2, uploads_controller.rb) will silently diverge on the next edit of any one of them.

[ADVISORY] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB as the server's limit regardless of the actual rejection reason. When the server rejects at its real configured limit (or rejects a non-image attachment at `max_attachment_size_kb`), the user is shown a 'file too large, max 10MB' message that misstates the actual policy, sending users to admins with wrong error reports.

[BUG] Animated-image detection inside `optimize` keys off the source filename matching `/\.GIF$/i`, but the new controller call site passes a Tempfile path like `/tmp/discourse-upload-composer20150101-123-abcd` with no extension. Animated GIFs routed through the new upload-downsize path never match the `_animated` instruction branch, so even when `allow_animation: true` is passed, the image is processed with the static (single-frame) downsize instructions, dropping all animation frames — the `allow_animation` option is dead at this call site.

[ADVISORY] The size gate uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` on the client-supplied/URL-derived filename while the actual bytes are what gets mutated, and the whole loop runs before any content-type verification by `Upload.create_for`. A client sending a non-image payload with an image-like filename (e.g. `photo.png` over the size limit) gets the file run through ImageMagick downsize on every upload attempt, using it as an unauthenticated image-transformation oracle on arbitrary bytes and, for a huge payload, five sequential shell-outs per request.

[BUG] The client-side max upload size check was changed from the admin-configurable SiteSetting to a hardcoded 10MB, silently discarding the existing operator control. Admins who set max_image_size_kb above or below 10MB are silently overridden; users on sites with a 2MB limit are told 10MB is allowed and get a confusing server-side failure, while sites wanting 20MB rejections now accept 20MB requests.

[BUG] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB instead of the actual SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the error message the user sees is wrong whenever the site setting differs. Users hitting the server's entity-too-large limit see a message quoting 10MB regardless of the real configured limit, making the guidance unactionable.

[BUG] The downsize loop shrinks pixel dimensions by 80% per iteration but tests tempfile.size (bytes), so a file whose bytes do not drop below max_image_size_kb within 5 iterations is uploaded anyway over the limit. A 9MB PNG with high entropy compresses poorly under 80% dimension scaling; after 5 attempts it may still exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and is passed to Upload.create_for, which then rejects it server-side or stores an oversized upload — the feature's stated goal (auto-reduce to allowed size) fails silently.

[BUG] The API URL download path now downloads up to a hardcoded 10.megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, changing the accepted remote-fetch bound without any admin control. An attacker with API access can make the server fetch and buffer 10MB remote payloads even on sites configured for 1MB, increasing bandwidth and memory exposure with no operator-configurable ceiling.

[ADVISORY] The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the literal string "80%" as dimensions, relying on ImageMagick accepting a percent geometry where every existing call site passes WxH — the intent ("80% of bytes") is expressed as "80% of dimensions". Future maintainers and the upload pipeline treat dimensions and bytes interchangeably; a non-image-but-detected-as-image or already-small-dimension file makes the loop converge on bytes slowly or never, and any caller refactor of optimize() assuming WxH geometry breaks this string.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a second definition of self.downsize (taking a dimensions string) immediately after the existing (max_width, max_height) version; Ruby silently keeps only the last definition, so the original arity-based method is dead and all existing callers passing two numeric args now raise ArgumentError. Every existing OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) call site — thumbnail generation, avatar resizing — raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking avatar/thumbnail generation site-wide.

[ADVISORY] The downsize writes output to tempfile.path while reading from tempfile.path (from == to), an in-place mutation the OptimizedImage API was never designed for. If convert fails mid-write or the animated-GIF instruction path builds a multi-step pipeline, the original upload data is corrupted/destroyed and the subsequent Upload.create_for stores a broken or zero-byte file.

[ADVISORY] The client-side file-size check is hardcoded to 10MB instead of reading the admin-configured SiteSetting, so the client enforces a limit the server does not share. When an admin sets max_image_size_kb (or max_attachment_size_kb) below 10MB, clients permit the upload and users hit a raw server rejection after the full transfer; when an admin raises it above 10MB, clients silently reject files the server would accept. The site operator's size policy is no longer enforced where users see it, and the 413 handler at line 246 has the same drift, promising a 10MB limit that is not the configured one.

[BUG] The downsize loop unconditionally invokes the shell/ImageMagick up to 5 times per upload even when downsize makes no progress or fails, with no check on the return value of convert_with. An attacker uploads (or passes via API URL) a file whose extension is an image type but whose content is not a valid image: is_image?(filename) is true, ImageMagick fails or leaves the file unchanged each iteration, and the server burns 5 synchronous shell invocations plus a full copy attempt per request. Chained across requests this is a CPU/process-exhaustion DoS on the upload path, and the upload then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file since nothing aborts on repeated failure.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination, running ImageMagick convert in-place on the upload tempfile. ImageMagick writing to its own input file can truncate or zero out the tempfile mid-operation on failure, so the user's original upload is silently destroyed and replaced with a corrupt/empty file that is then passed to Upload.create_for — data loss of the user's upload with a confusing server error instead of a clean 'file too large' rejection.

[ADVISORY] Animated-GIF detection matches the source path against /\.GIF$/i, but the new call site passes a tempfile whose name is 'discourse-upload-<type>' with no .gif extension (the extension lives only in the separately-derived filename variable). Every animated GIF downloaded via the API URL path or uploaded through this new loop is processed with the non-animated instruction set (the _animated variant that honors allow_animated_thumbnails is never selected), so animated uploads take the wrong processing branch — frames are flattened or the allow_animated_thumbnails site setting is bypassed for exactly the files it governs.

[ADVISORY] The image check trusts FileHelper.is_image?(filename) where filename is the attacker-controlled basename of the API-supplied URL, so the server-side downsize loop gates on client-controlled extension, not content. The newly added heavy server-side processing (up to 5 ImageMagick invocations) is reachable for any content an API caller labels with an image extension, including decompression-bomb images and non-image payloads, widening the surface of unvetted content handed to ImageMagick on a request path that previously did no processing.

[BUG] `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same module body, so the second definition silently replaces the first and the four-argument width/height signature is dead. Any existing caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) — the signature the rest of the Discourse codebase was written against (e.g. thumbnail/cooked-image generation paths) — now hits the second definition, where the `dimensions` parameter receives only `max_width`; the geometry string becomes e.g. "1920" with no height and no trailing 'x', producing malformed ImageMagick instructions and failed/broken image resizes everywhere the old call form is used. The first definition is unreachable dead code that misleads every future reader.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination (in-place convert), and convert_with's false return on ImageMagick failure is ignored. Users uploading large images: `convert in.png out.png` with identical paths is documented-unsafe in ImageMagick (output can be written while input is still being read, corrupting the file), and when the shell command fails (corrupt image, missing convert binary) the loop keeps iterating on an unchanged tempfile and the oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway, surfacing as an opaque 500 instead of a size error.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size check hardcodes 10MB, discarding the SiteSetting-driven max_image_size_kb that the server still enforces for non-images (and for images when the server downsize loop fails). Admins who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB: users are told up-front that files up to 10MB are acceptable, then hit a server-side rejection for non-image files (or oversized images whose downsize failed), replacing a clear pre-upload message with a worse post-upload error; admins who raise the setting above 10MB get files silently blocked client-side below the real limit.

[ADVISORY] The fixed 5-iteration downsize loop with '80%' geometry has no convergence guarantee and is not bounded by the actual required size, only by attempt count. A user uploading a very large image (e.g. 50MB with max_image_size_kb set low) can still exceed the limit after 5 iterations (0.8^5 ≈ 33% reduction), and the file is then passed to Upload.create_for anyway, causing the server-side size validation error the feature was supposed to eliminate.

[BUG] The downsize loop overwrites the user's original image in place (from and to are both tempfile.path), destroying the original file before the upload is validated or persisted. ImageMagick 'convert in.png in.png' reads and writes the same file; on a failed or partial conversion (or when the 5 attempts still leave a file exceeding max_image_size_kb and the upload is then rejected by size validation), the tempfile is left truncated, corrupted, or zero-size — the user's original image bytes are permanently lost and no upload is created, forcing the user to re-supply a file they can no longer recover from the server.

[BUG] The diff defines self.downsize twice within the same class body — def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) followed by def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) — so the first definition (and its width/height interpolation) is silently dead code and Ruby emits a 'method redefined' warning. Any caller still using the old 4-argument arity (width, height) now flows into the dimensions-arity body, where max_width is stringified as "#{max_width}x#{max_height}" with max_height landing in opts — existing callers passing numeric width/height plus opts get their opts hash shifted, so opts like allow_animation is silently lost and dimensions are built from the wrong values; the next maintainer also cannot tell which signature is authoritative.

[ADVISORY] Removing the public helper self.dimensions(width, height) is a silent public-surface change with no in-file callers left, but it is an exported class method on a core model. Any plugin or out-of-tree caller invoking OptimizedImage.dimensions(w, h) now raises NoMethodError at runtime after this deploy, with no deprecation path; this is also the mechanism that hides the duplicate-downsize confusion above.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop has no success check: OptimizedImage.downsize (via convert_with) returns false on convert failure, but the loop ignores the return value and re-reads tempfile.size, so a repeatedly failing conversion spins all 5 attempts against an unmodified (or corrupted) file and then proceeds to create the upload anyway. Users uploading an image ImageMagick cannot process get 5 wasted shell invocations per upload attempt and, because the in-place write may have truncated the file, Upload.create_for is called with a size argument (tempfile.size) that no longer matches the file content — the stored upload metadata disagrees with the stored bytes.

[ADVISORY] The client-side max size check is hardcoded to 10MB instead of reading SiteSetting max_image_size_kb, while the server still enforces the site setting. On sites with max_image_size_kb set below 10240, users are told 10MB is allowed, pick a file under 10MB, and the downsize loop runs; if the loop cannot compress enough in 5 iterations the server-side validation rejects the upload — the user sees a failure after the client explicitly promised the file was acceptable, and the i18n message reports a wrong limit.

[BUG] The new 3-arg `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` redefines the same method as the 4-arg version declared directly above it, and Ruby keeps only the last definition, so every existing caller passing (from, to, width, height, opts) now lands in the 3-arg method with dimensions=width and opts=height (an Integer). Any pre-existing call like `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, to, 100, 200, allow_animation: true)` raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` at `opts[:allow_animation]` inside optimize, breaking avatar/optimized-image generation with a 500 wherever the width/height form is used.

[BUG] The downsize loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s return value (convert_with returns false on ImageMagick failure) and never checks after the loop that the file is actually under the limit, so it proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with either an unchanged or still-oversized tempfile. When ImageMagick fails (bad image, corrupt file, missing binary), the loop burns 5 attempts silently, the original oversized file is passed through, and the user gets a generic size-validation error (or, if server limits allow, an unshrunk upload) with no log of the conversion failure — the feature silently no-ops.

[BUG] Five iterations of a fixed `"80%"` downsize can only shrink dimensions to ~33% of the original, so any image whose pixel count is large relative to the byte limit (e.g. a 20MP PNG against max_image_size_kb of 500) still exceeds the limit when the loop exits. The upload is then rejected by the existing size validation after spending 5 sequential ImageMagick invocations, and the user receives a 'file too large' error for a feature that was supposed to make this upload succeed — silent partial success of the resize loop.

[BUG] The client-side hardcodes `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`, discarding the SiteSetting-driven `max_ + type + _size_kb` check, so the validation message and gate no longer reflect the actual server limit for any upload type. On sites with max_image_size_kb above 10MB, users are blocked client-side with a wrong 'max 10MB' message for files the server would accept; conversely sites with a limit below 10MB rely on a server roundtrip (or the 413 path) for rejection — the pre-upload check is now silently wrong in both directions.

[ADVISORY] The animated-GIF branch in `optimize` (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) is selected by the source filename, but here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which is the extension-less `discourse-upload-#{type}` path. Every animated GIF uploaded through this new path takes the non-animated downsize instructions, so `allow_animated_thumbnails` is silently ineffective and animated uploads are processed with the static pipeline (potentially mangling the file) — the setting's behavior is skipped with no error.

[ADVISORY] The 413 handler message now hardcodes 10MB instead of reading the site setting, so the error text no longer matches the server that actually returned 413. Users on sites where the web server's actual limit differs from 10MB (e.g. nginx client_max_body_size) get a misdirecting message that misdescribes the real constraint, sending debugging in the wrong direction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loop downsizes in place (from == to: tempfile.path passed as both source and destination), and ImageMagick `convert in.gif out.gif` with identical input/output paths truncates the file mid-read, producing a corrupt/empty image when a single pass would have sufficed. Users uploading large GIFs get a corrupted upload stored and served instead of a downsized one.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, passing the same file path as both `from` and `to` repeatedly. The diff shows no safeguard (e.g., using a separate temp output file + rename) against in-place conversion, so the finding that this can corrupt/truncate the file when ImageMagick writes to the same path it reads from is a plausible, diff-grounded correctness issue affecting uploads (especially in the repeated loop).

[BUG] The auto-downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of 80% scaling (0.8^5 ≈ 33% of original area), so any image larger than ~3x the configured max_image_size_kb exits the loop still over the limit and the upload fails anyway — the feature's promise of 'automatically downsize large images' silently fails for exactly the largest images it targets. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop that retries at most 5 times, each time calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. The finding’s key claim (that 5 iterations only get you to ~33% of original *area* and thus fails for files >~3x the max) is not supported: 0.8^5 ≈ 0.33 is a *linear* scale factor; pixel area would be ~0.11, implying up to ~9x reduction if size roughly follows pixel count. The specific example (12MB -> 2MB still failing) is also not grounded in the diff; additionally, the client-side cap was changed to 10MB (`10*1024` KB), so 12MB is not an in-scope case for normal uploads per this diff. While it’s possible some very large-to-max ratios could still fail after 5 tries, the finding’s quantitative threshold and example are incorrect based on what the diff shows.

A PNG or animation whose compressed size does not shrink proportionally with dimensions (palette-heavy PNGs, animated GIFs) exits the loop after 5 attempts still over `max_image_size_kb`, and the upload then fails with the same unhelpful oversized error the feature was supposed to eliminate — while also having needlessly degraded a merely-slightly-over-limit image to ~33% of its area (0.8^5) even when one 95% step would have sufficed.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop downsizes images by repeatedly calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` up to 5 times, but after the loop it does not verify success (still-over-limit case) or handle failure differently; it proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` regardless. From the diff alone we can verify the fixed-step loop and the lack of a post-loop check/branch, which can lead to unnecessary extra degradation and still passing an oversized file onward. The claim that the upload "fails with the same error" depends on `Upload.create_for` behavior not shown here, so that part isn’t fully verifiable.

In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize/optimize` ultimately builds a shell `convert` command via `convert_with(instructions, to)` and only checks `$?.exitstatus`. The diff shows no atomic temp output or copy, so the downsize overwrites the tempfile in-place; if `convert` partially writes/truncates when input==output or if later `Upload.create_for` fails, the server-side original bytes are already replaced, and there’s no recorded original to fall back to.
